title: Harmonic Form
page_title: Harmonic Form | Edexcel International A Level (IAL) Maths Revision Notes 2020

blocks.name: R addition formulae Rcos Rsin etc

blocks.md:
- If ***a*** and ***b*** are positive constants, then

  - ***a *****sin *****x *****+ *****b*****cos *****x*** can be rewritten as ***R *****sin (*****x *****+ α)**
  - ***a *****sin *****x *****- *****b*****cos *****x*** can be rewritten as ***R *****sin (*****x *****- α)**
  - ***a *****cos *****x *****+ *****b*****sin *****x*** can be rewritten as ***R *****cos (*****x *****- α)**
  - ***a *****cos *****x *****- *****b*****sin *****x*** can be rewritten as ***R *****cos (*****x *****+ α)**
- The forms with ***R*** and **α **are called **harmonic forms**

  - It is the reverse of expanding the right-hand side out using compound angle formulae
  - It can be seen as factorising
- In all four cases ***R *****> 0** and **0 < α < 90°**, with:

blocks.alt: Rcos(x+a) Illustr 1, A Level & AS Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md:
- To find **α**,** **first divide the **b** expression by the **a** expression

  - The ***R***'s cancel
  - Use the identity sin **α** / cos **α** = tan **α**
  - You get** b / a = tan** **α **
  - Then use** tan**<sup>**-1**</sup>** (b/a) **to find **α **

blocks.text: How do I write trigonometric expressions in harmonic form?

blocks.md: - To rewrite the expression use the appropriate **compound angle formula** and equate coefficients ![maths-homepage-image-new](assets/ce86d53fd57c-maths-homepage-image-new.png)

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: - There is more than one way to rewrite a given expression, and the question in the exam will tell you which form to use.
